questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an exception to the 'Law of Demand'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Substitute goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Demand**, popularized by **Alfred Marshall** in **1890**, states that there is an **inverse relationship** between the **price** of a good and its **quantity demanded**, assuming all other factors remain constant.
 
• **Giffen goods** are a unique category of **inferior goods** (such as **staple foods** like **bread** or **potatoes**) where the **income effect** is stronger than the **substitution effect**. When the **price** of a Giffen good **rises**, consumers, being too poor to afford expensive substitutes, actually buy more of the staple good. ***Hence, statement A is an exception to the law.***
 
• **Conspicuous goods**, also known as **Veblen goods** named after **Thorstein Veblen**, are **luxury items** like **designer watches**, **luxury cars**, or **diamonds**. These goods are purchased for **status** or **snob appeal**; as their **price increases**, they become more **exclusive** and **desirable**, leading to higher **demand**. ***Hence, statement B is an exception to the law.***
 
• **Speculative goods** involve assets where buyers **anticipate** future **price movements**. In **stock markets** or **real estate**, if the **price** of an asset **rises**, investors often buy more of it expecting the **price** to rise further in the **future** to secure a **profit**. ***Hence, statement C is an exception to the law.***
 
• **Substitute goods** are products that can replace each other, such as **Tea and Coffee** or **Pepsi and Coca-Cola**. While the **price** of one substitute affects the **demand** for another (**positive cross-price elasticity**), each good individually follows the standard **Law of Demand**; if the **price** of **Tea** rises, the **quantity demanded** for **Tea** itself will **fall**. ***Hence, statement D is NOT an exception to the law.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cross-Price Elasticity**: This measures the **responsiveness** of the **quantity demanded** for one good to a **change in the price** of another good. For **substitute goods**, this value is **positive**, meaning an **increase** in the **price** of **Coffee** leads to an **increase** in the **demand** for **Tea**.
 
• **Veblen Effect**: First identified in the **1899** book **"The Theory of the Leisure Class"**, it describes **conspicuous consumption** where **utility** is derived from the **exhibit of wealth** rather than the **functional use** of the product.
 
• **Giffen Paradox**: Observed by **Sir Robert Giffen** during the **19th century** in **Ireland**, he noticed that a rise in the **price** of **potatoes** caused the **poor** to consume more of them because they had to cut back on **expensive meat** to afford the **basic staple**.
 
• **Complementary Goods**: These are goods used together, such as **Cars and Petrol** or **Printers and Ink Cartridges**. Unlike substitutes, they have a **negative cross-price elasticity**; if the **price** of **petrol** rises, the **demand** for **cars** typically **decreases**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Demand Curve Shape**: While a **normal demand curve** slopes **downward from left to right**, the demand curve for **exceptions** like **Giffen** or **Veblen goods** slopes **upward**, indicating a **direct relationship** between **price** and **quantity**.
 
• **Consumer Ignorance**: Sometimes, **consumers** judge the **quality** of a product by its **price**. They may buy more of a **high-priced product** assuming it is of **superior quality**, which acts as another **psychological exception** to the law.
 
• **Emergency Situations**: During times of **war**, **famine**, or **pandemics**, people tend to **hoard goods** even when **prices** are **skyrocketing** due to **fear of shortage**, bypassing the traditional **Law of Demand**.
 
• **Necessary Goods**: For **life-saving medicines** or **salt**, the **quantity demanded** remains relatively **stable** regardless of **price changes**, showing **low price elasticity**.
</ul

questions.question: What is a modern trend regarding business licenses?

options.text: Increasing the amount of time it takes to get them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Making them easier to obtain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The modern trend globally and in **India** is toward the **liberalization** and **simplification** of business regulations. Governments are increasingly focusing on the **Ease of Doing Business** to attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** and foster **entrepreneurship**. ***Hence, the option "Making them easier to obtain" is correct.***
 
• Technological integration has led to the development of **online portals** and **digital platforms** where entrepreneurs can apply for and receive licenses without physical visits to government offices, reducing **bureaucratic red tape**.
 
• The concept of a **"Single Window Clearance"** system has been adopted by many nations to provide all necessary approvals (environmental, labor, tax, and local permits) through a **single interface**, significantly reducing the **time** and **cost** of starting a business.
 
• Reducing **compliance burdens** is a key feature of modern economic policies, ensuring that **Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)** can operate efficiently without being overwhelmed by excessive **administrative requirements**.
 
• Instead of removing licenses altogether (which might compromise safety or health standards) or making them impossible to obtain, the trend is to make the **regulatory environment** more **transparent** and **predictable**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP):** In **India**, the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)** releases the **BRAP** rankings for states based on their implementation of reforms. This creates a **competitive federalism** model to improve the business climate at the **regional level**.
 
• **SPICe+ Form:** The **Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)** introduced the **SPICe+** (Simplified Proforma for Incorporating Company Electronically Plus) web form. It integrates **11 services** from **three Central Government Ministries** and departments, drastically cutting down the **number of days** required to incorporate a **company**.
 
• **National Single Window System (NSWS):** Launched in **September 2021**, this digital platform serves as a **one-stop-shop** for investors. It allows them to identify, apply for, and track **approvals** according to their specific **business requirements** across **Central** and **State** governments.
 
• **World Bank Rankings:** Historically, the **World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Index** influenced many countries to reform their licensing procedures. High-ranking countries like **Singapore** and **New Zealand** are known for allowing businesses to start in less than **24 to 48 hours**.
 
• **Impact on MSMEs:** Simplified licensing is particularly beneficial for the **MSME sector**, which contributes nearly **30%** to **India's GDP** and is a major source of **employment** for the **youth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Self-Certification:** A significant modern feature is the introduction of **self-certification** and **third-party inspections**. Businesses can declare their own **compliance** with certain standards, and **physical audits** are conducted only based on **risk-profiling** rather than routine schedules.
 
• **De-criminalization of Laws:** Recent trends involve the **de-criminalization** of minor technical or procedural lapses under the **Companies Act, 2013**, and various **labor laws**. This prevents the fear of **imprisonment** for honest entrepreneurs over **numerical errors** or **filing delays**.
 
• **Validity and Renewals:** Many licenses are now issued with **longer validity periods** or even **lifetime validity**. This moves away from the **annual renewal** cycles of the **"License Raj"** era, which were often associated with **corruption** and **administrative delays**.
 
• **Time-Bound Delivery:** Several states in **India** have enacted the **Right to Public Services Act**, which mandates the **time-bound delivery** of business permits. If a **license** is not granted within a specific **statutory period** (e.g., **30 days**), it is often considered **"deemed approved"**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the CORRECT objective of ISRO's Gaganyaan mission scheduled for launch in 2025?

options.text: Sending Indian astronauts into low-Earth orbit
Sending an unmanned rover to the Moon
Launching a solar probe to study the Sun

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sending Indian astronauts into low-Earth orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary objective of the **Gaganyaan Mission** is to demonstrate **India's** indigenous capability to undertake human spaceflight to **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**. It aims to send a **3-member crew** to an altitude of **400 km** for a mission duration of **3 days**. ***Hence, option B is correct.***
 
• The mission is being spearheaded by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and was first formally announced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** during his **Independence Day speech** in **2018**.
 
• The launch vehicle identified for the **Gaganyaan** mission is the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-III)**, which was previously known as **GSLV Mk III**. This heavy-lift launcher consists of **solid, liquid, and cryogenic stages** and has been re-configured to meet **human-rating** requirements.
 
• Success in this mission will make **India** the **fourth country** in the world to launch a manned space mission, following the **Soviet Union (now Russia)**, the **United States**, and **China**.
 
• The mission also involves a safe return to **Earth**, where the **Crew Module** will splash down in **Indian sea waters** (likely the **Arabian Sea**) after re-entry into the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Crew Selection and Training:** The four designated **Gaganyatris** (astronaut-designates) are **Group Captain Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair**, **Group Captain Ajit Krishnan**, **Group Captain Angad Pratap**, and **Wing Commander Shubhanshu Shukla**, all from the **Indian Air Force (IAF)**. They underwent rigorous training at the **Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Center** in **Russia** and are now training at **ISRO's Astronaut Training Facility** in **Bengaluru**.
 
• **Vyommitra (The Humanoid):** Before the actual crewed flight, **ISRO** will launch uncrewed missions carrying a **female robot humanoid** named **Vyommitra**. Her role is to simulate human functions, monitor **module parameters**, and alert about **environmental changes** within the capsule to ensure crew safety.
 
• **Human Rated LVM3 (HLVM3):** This specialized version of the **LVM3** rocket includes a **Crew Escape System (CES)** powered by high-burn rate solid motors, ensuring the **Crew Module** can be pulled away to safety in case of any **launch pad** or **ascent-phase** emergencies.
 
• **Orbital Module:** It consists of two parts: the **Crew Module (CM)**, which is the habitable space with an **Earth-like environment** for the astronauts, and the **Service Module (SM)**, which provides the necessary **propulsion** and **power** during the orbital phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Test Vehicle Missions (TV-D1):** On **October 21, 2023**, **ISRO** successfully conducted the **Flight Test Vehicle Abort Mission-1 (TV-D1)** from **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**. This test validated the performance of the **Crew Escape System** at a **Mach number of 1.2**.
 
• **Future Space Milestones:** The **Gaganyaan** mission is a foundational step toward establishing the **Bharatiya Antariksha Station (BAS)**, a permanent Indian space station planned for **2035**, and the eventual goal of landing an **Indian on the Moon** by **2040**.
 
• **Critical Technologies:** Development involves **Thermal Protection Systems** to withstand high temperatures during re-entry, **Life Support Systems** to provide **Oxygen** and remove **Carbon Dioxide**, and **Navigation, Guidance, and Control (NGC)** systems.
 
• **Economic and Scientific Impact:** The project, with a budget of approximately **₹9,023 Crore**, encourages **industrial participation** (both **public and private**) and inspires **STEM** education among the youth in **India**.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios best illustrates the principle of conservation of momentum?

options.text: A ball rolling down a frictionless incline increases its speed.
A car comes to a stop when the brakes are applied due to friction.
When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils in the opposite direction.
A satellite maintains a stable orbit around the Earth due to gravity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils in the opposite direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Law of Conservation of Momentum** states that the total **linear momentum** of a closed or **isolated system** remains constant if no **external force** acts on it. Momentum is defined as the product of an object's **mass** and its **velocity**.

• **Statement 1:** A ball rolling down a **frictionless incline** increases its speed because of the **external force** of **gravity** acting along the slope. Since an external force is accelerating the ball, the **momentum** of the ball is not conserved; it increases as the **velocity** increases. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 2:** When a car comes to a stop due to **brakes**, the **external force** of **friction** between the tires and the **road** acts on the vehicle. This force changes the **momentum** of the car from its initial value to **zero**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 3:** When a **bullet** is fired from a **gun**, the system (gun + bullet) is initially at rest with a total **momentum** of **zero**. Upon firing, the **internal force** of the exploding gunpowder pushes the bullet forward and the gun backward. The forward **momentum** of the bullet is exactly balanced by the backward **recoil momentum** of the gun, keeping the total **system momentum** at **zero**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• **Statement 4:** A **satellite** in a stable **orbit** is subject to the **external gravitational force** of the **Earth**. While the magnitude of its **velocity** (speed) might remain constant in a circular orbit, its direction is constantly changing due to **centripetal force**, meaning its **vector momentum** is continuously changing. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Mathematical Expression:** The principle is mathematically represented as **m1u1 + m2u2 = m1v1 + m2v2**, where **m** represents **mass**, **u** represents **initial velocity**, and **v** represents **final velocity** of the interacting bodies.

• **Newton’s Third Law Connection:** The conservation of **momentum** is a direct consequence of **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**, which states that for every action, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. The forces between the bullet and the gun are internal **action-reaction pairs**.

• **Types of Collisions:** In **physics**, momentum is conserved in both **elastic** and **inelastic collisions**. However, **kinetic energy** is only conserved in **elastic collisions** (like ideal **gas molecules** or **billiard balls**), while it is partially converted to **heat** or **sound** in inelastic ones.

• **Applications:** This principle is fundamental in **rocket propulsion**. A **rocket** moves upward by ejecting **exhaust gases** downward at high **velocity**. The downward **momentum** of the gases provides an equal upward **momentum** to the rocket body.

• **Vector Nature:** Since **velocity** is a **vector**, **momentum** is also a **vector quantity**. This means that in **two-dimensional** or **three-dimensional** space, the **momentum** must be conserved independently along the **x, y, and z axes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **System Definition:** For the conservation law to apply, one must clearly define the **isolated system**. In the gun-bullet example, if we only look at the bullet, its **momentum** is not conserved because the gun exerts a **force** on it. Conservation only applies when both objects are treated as a **single unit**.

• **Recoil Velocity:** The **recoil velocity** of a **gun** is much smaller than the **muzzle velocity** of the **bullet** because the **mass** of the gun is significantly larger than the **mass** of the bullet, as shown by the relation **V_gun = -(m_bullet * v_bullet) / M_gun**.

• **Impulse:** The change in **momentum** is known as **impulse**. When an **external force** is applied over a **time interval**, the **momentum** changes according to the **Impulse-Momentum Theorem** (**Force × Time = ΔMomentum**).

• **Historical Context:** While the concept of **momentum** was discussed by earlier scientists like **Descartes**, it was **Sir Isaac Newton** who formalized these laws in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** published in **1687**.

questions.question: The National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) was initiated in the ________ Five-Year Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixth Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Rural Employment Programme (NREP)** was launched in **October 1980** during the **Sixth Five-Year Plan**. It was designed to replace the earlier **Food for Work Programme** to streamline employment generation in rural sectors.
 
• The primary objective of the **NREP** was to generate additional gainful employment for the unemployed and underemployed persons in the rural areas of **India**.
 
• This programme aimed at the creation of **durable community assets** for strengthening the rural infrastructure, such as **rural roads**, **school buildings**, and **panchayat ghars**.
 
• The funding for the **National Rural Employment Programme** was shared between the **Central Government** and the **State Governments** on a **50:50** basis.
 
• Under this initiative, a specific target was set to generate **300 to 400 million mandays** of employment per annum for the rural poor to ensure food security and income stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–1985):**
 
 
• The **Sixth Five-Year Plan** marked the beginning of economic liberalization in **India** and focused heavily on **poverty alleviation** and **economic self-reliance**.
 
• The plan was launched under the leadership of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi** with a target growth rate of **5.2%**, but it successfully achieved a growth rate of **5.7%**.
 
• It emphasized **family planning** to control the growing **population** and invested significantly in the **energy sector** and **agriculture**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Employment Schemes:**
 
 
• In **1983**, during the same plan period, the **Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP)** was introduced to provide a guarantee of employment to at least one member of every landless household for up to **100 days** in a **year**.
 
• Later, on **April 1, 1989**, both **NREP** and **RLEGP** were merged to form the **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY)**, which became a major flagship employment scheme.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1978):**
 
 
• This plan focused on **'Garibi Hatao'** (Removal of Poverty) and **Justice**. It was terminated **one year** early in **1978** by the **Janata Party government**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)** was another crucial scheme launched in **1980** to provide self-employment opportunities to the rural poor through **subsidies** and **bank loans**.
 
• The **National Rural Employment Programme** prioritized the **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** for employment, ensuring that a portion of the funds was reserved for their **socio-economic development**.
 
• The **Sixth Plan** is often cited as the **'Plan of Infrastructure'** as it significantly expanded **irrigation projects** and **national highways** across the **country**.
 
• Currently, the spirit of these early employment programmes is carried forward by the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, which was enacted in **2005** to provide a legal **Right to Work**.

questions.question: The first peptide to be produced after wounding in the tomato plant is ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Systemin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Systemin** is an **18-amino acid peptide** that acts as a primary signaling molecule in **tomato plants** (**Solanum lycopersicum**) and other members of the **Solanaceae** family. It was the **first peptide hormone** ever discovered in plants, identified in **1991** by the research team led by **Clarence A. Ryan**.
 
• The peptide is released from a much larger precursor protein called **prosystemin**, which contains **200 amino acids**. Upon **wounding** caused by **herbivorous insects** or mechanical damage, prosystemin is proteolytically processed to release the active **systemin**.
 
• Its primary function is to mediate the **systemic wound response**. Once released at the site of injury, it travels through the **phloem** to distant leaves, acting as a long-distance signal to prepare the entire plant for potential further attack.
 
• In the target cells, **Systemin** binds to a **cell surface receptor** (**SR160**, a member of the **Leucine-Rich Repeat Receptor-Like Kinase** family). This binding triggers a signaling cascade that activates the **octadecanoid pathway**, eventually leading to the synthesis of **Jasmonic Acid**.
 
• The ultimate result of this signaling is the **induction of defense genes**, most notably those encoding **Protease Inhibitors (PIs)**. These inhibitors interfere with the **digestive enzymes** of insects, making the plant tissues indigestible and deterring further feeding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jasmonic Acid (JA):**
 
 
• **Jasmonic acid** is a **lipid-derived hormone** synthesized from **linolenic acid** via the **octadecanoid pathway**. While it is crucial for wounding defense, it is a **small molecule hormone**, not a peptide. It works downstream of **Systemin** to activate the **transcription** of defense proteins.
 
 
 
• **Salicylic Acid (SA):**
 
 
• **Salicylic acid** is a **phenolic phytohormone** primarily involved in **Systemic Acquired Resistance (SAR)**. It plays a major role in defending the plant against **biotrophic pathogens** (which feed on living tissue). Unlike systemin, which responds to **chewing insects**, SA is the lead signal for **microbial infections**.
 
 
 
• **Ricin:**
 
 
• **Ricin** is a highly potent **toxin** found in the **seeds** of the **Castor oil plant** (**Ricinus communis**). It is a **Type II ribosome-inactivating protein (RIP)** that inhibits **protein synthesis** in eukaryotic cells. It is **not a signaling peptide** involved in tomato plant wounding but is a chemical defense against ingestion.
 
 
 
• **Ethylene:**
 
 
• **Ethylene** is a **gaseous plant hormone** that often works in synergy with **Jasmonic acid** during the wound response. It is involved in **fruit ripening**, **senescence**, and **abscission**, as well as reacting to **necrotrophic pathogens**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **discovery of Systemin** challenged the long-held belief that plant hormones were only **small molecules** like **auxins**, **gibberellins**, and **cytokinins**. It established that **peptides** could also serve as potent **long-distance messengers** in plants.
 
• **Phloem transport:** The ability of **Systemin** to move through the **sieve tubes** of the **phloem** allows the plant to coordinate a **whole-body defense** within **hours** of an localized attack.
 
• **Specificity:** While **Systemin** is specific to **Solanaceous** plants, other plant families use different **Peptide Elucidators (Peps)** to achieve similar **immune responses**.
</ul

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which of the following has been emphasized for the first time in criminal law regarding sexual offences?

options.text: Marital rape as a punishable offense
Consent must be explicitly defined and recorded
Death penalty for all rape cases
Gender neutrality in sexual assault definitions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gender neutrality in sexual assault definitions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**, which replaced the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** of **1860**, has introduced a significant shift by emphasizing **gender neutrality** in several definitions related to sexual assault and victims. While the core definition of rape under **Section 63** remains largely gender-specific (perpetrated by a man), the BNS 2023 moves toward recognizing **transgender persons** and uses more inclusive language in various sections related to sexual offenses. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• One of the most notable additions is **Section 69**, which specifically criminalizes sexual intercourse through **deceitful means** or a **false promise to marry**. This is the first time such an offense has been codified with a distinct punishment of up to **10 years** of **imprisonment**, moving away from the previous ambiguity in the **IPC**.
 
• The **BNS 2023** prioritizes offenses against **women and children** by placing them in **Chapter 5** of the code. This structural change signifies the legislature's intent to give paramount importance to these crimes compared to the **IPC**, where such offenses were placed much later in the document.
 
• Regarding **marital rape**, the **BNS 2023** retains the **exception** (Exception 2 to Section 63) which states that sexual intercourse by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under **18 years** of age, is not rape. Therefore, marital rape has not been made a punishable offense under this new Sanhita. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• While the **death penalty** is a possible punishment under **Section 70(2)** for the **gang rape** of a girl under **18 years** of age, it is not prescribed for "all" rape cases. The law maintains a hierarchy of punishments based on the severity and age of the victim. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

However, this definition was already evolved through the **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013**; thus, it is not a "first time" inclusion in **2023**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Aggravated Punishment:** The **BNS 2023** increases the minimum punishment for **rape** from **7 years** to **10 years** of **rigorous imprisonment**. For the **gang rape** of a woman, the punishment is **imprisonment for life** (which means the remainder of that person's natural life) or **rigorous imprisonment** for a term not less than **20 years**.
 
• **Protection of Minors:** The new code emphasizes the protection of **children** (defined as anyone under **18 years**). Crimes against children carry much more stringent penalties, including the **death penalty** or **life imprisonment** without the possibility of remission in specific aggravated cases.
 
• **Community Service:** For the first time in Indian criminal law, the **BNS 2023** introduces **Community Service** as a form of **punishment** for petty offenses, aiming at a more **reformative** approach to justice rather than purely **retributive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Section 63 (Rape):** Replaces **Section 375** of the **IPC**. It maintains the **four-step** definition of the act but adds clarity to the **punitive measures** in subsequent sections.
 
• **Section 70 (Gang Rape):** Specifically deals with **gang rape**, providing a minimum of **20 years** of imprisonment or **life imprisonment**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a traditional dance of Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Theyyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Theyyam** is a popular ritual dance form of **Kerala**, predominantly performed in the **North Malabar** region, including districts like **Kannur**, **Kasaragod**, **Wayanad**, and **Kozhikode**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• It is an ancient art form that encompasses **dance**, **mime**, and **music**, and it is performed to worship heroes and ancestral spirits. The word **Theyyam** is a corruption of **Daivam**, which means **God** in **Malayalam**.
 
• **Dhol Cholom** is a traditional folk dance from the state of **Manipur**, performed during the **Yaoshang** festival (Holi) using large drums called **Dhols**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Giddha** is a popular folk dance of **Punjab**, specifically performed by **women** during social gatherings and festivals like **Teeyan** to celebrate the harvest. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• **Bhangra** is a high-energy folk dance originating from the **Majha** area of **Punjab**. It is traditionally performed by **men** during the **Vaisakhi** festival to celebrate the **harvest** season. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Theyyam:**

 
 
• There are approximately **400** distinct types of Theyyam, each with its own unique **music**, **style**, and **choreography**. Some famous ones include **Raktha Chamundi**, **Kari Chamundi**, and **Muchilottu Bhagavathi**.
 
• The performers belong to specific indigenous communities such as the **Vannan**, **Malayan**, **Mavilan**, and **Velan**.
 
• The performance usually takes place in **sacred groves** known as **Kavu** or in front of village shrines. The ritual involves the performer "becoming" the deity after wearing the elaborate costume and mask.
 
 
 
• **Dhol Cholom (Manipur):**
 
 
• This dance is characterized by **acrobatic** movements and the rhythmic beating of the **Dhol**. It is often performed as a prelude to other dances during the **Holi** festivities.
 
• It showcases the **physical stamina** and **rhythmic precision** of the dancers in the **Meitei** culture.
 
 
 
• **Giddha and Bhangra (Punjab):**
 
 
• **Giddha** features **Boliyan** (folk verses) and rhythmic **clapping**, displaying the grace and femininity of the dancers.
 
• **Bhangra** has evolved into a global phenomenon, often performed at **weddings** and **celebrations**, involving energetic steps like the **double-hop** and **shoulder shrugs**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Classical Dances of Kerala:**

 
 
• **Kathakali:** A world-famous classical dance-drama known for its heavy **costumes**, **makeup**, and **mudras** (hand gestures).
 
• **Mohiniyattam:** A solo classical dance performed by **women**, characterized by graceful, swaying movements like the **waves of the ocean**.
 
 
 
• **Ritual Arts:**
 
 
• **Koodiyattam** from **Kerala** is the only surviving form of **Sanskrit theatre** in India and is recognized by **UNESCO** as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.
 
• The **Theyyam** season usually begins in the **Malayalam month** of **Thulam** (October/November) and continues until **Idavam** (May/June).

questions.question:
Which of the following products are part of the petrochemical industry in India?
1. Polymers
2. Synthetic fibres
3. Elastomers
4. Surfactant intermediates
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, 3 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Polymers** are a dominant segment of the **petrochemical industry**, consisting of long-chain molecules produced through **polymerization**. These include **Polyethylene (PE)**, **Polypropylene (PP)**, and **Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC)**, which are utilized in **packaging**, **infrastructure**, and **automotive parts**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Synthetic fibres** are man-made fibres created from **petrochemical sources** like **Ethylene** and **Para-xylene**. Major types in India include **Polyester**, **Nylon**, and **Acrylic**, which are critical for the **textile sector** and **industrial fabrics**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Elastomers** refer to synthetic polymers with elastic properties, commonly known as **synthetic rubber**. Products like **Styrene-Butadiene Rubber (SBR)** and **Polybutadiene Rubber (PBR)** are essential for the **automobile industry** in the manufacturing of **tyres** and **tubes**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Surfactant intermediates** are chemical compounds used as precursors for **detergents** and **cleaning agents**. The most prominent example is **Linear Alkyl Benzene (LAB)**, which is derived from **n-paraffins** and **benzene**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overview of Petrochemical Industry**: The industry involves the transformation of **crude oil** and **natural gas** into useful products. **India** is the **6th largest** producer of chemicals globally and accounts for approximately **7%** of the global market share in the **chemical industry**.
 
• **Feedstocks**: The primary feedstocks used in the Indian petrochemical sector are **Naphtha**, **Natural Gas**, and **Ethane**. These are cracked to produce **olefins** (like **Ethylene** and **Propylene**) and **aromatics** (like **Benzene** and **Toluene**).
 
• **Government Policy**: The **Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemical Investment Regions (PCPIR)** policy aims to establish clusters for manufacturing. Notable regions include **Dahej** in **Gujarat**, **Paradip** in **Odisha**, and **Visakhapatnam** in **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• **Market Trends**: The Indian market is seeing a shift towards **Specialty Chemicals**, which find applications in **pharmaceuticals**, **agrochemicals**, and **electronics**. The sector is projected to grow at a **CAGR** of around **10-12%** by **2030**.
 
• **Major Players**: The industry is led by giants like **Reliance Industries Limited (RIL)**, **Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL)**, and **GAIL (India) Limited**, which operate large-scale **cracker plants** across the **country**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals**: This department, under the **Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers**, is the nodal agency for policy and planning. It oversees the **National Policy on Petrochemicals**, which aims to improve global competitiveness.
 
• **Environmental Regulations**: The industry is subject to strict guidelines by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** regarding **effluent treatment** and **carbon emissions**, promoting **sustainable manufacturing** practices.
 
• **Import Dependence**: Despite high production, India still imports certain **specialty polymers** and **intermediates**. The **Make in India** initiative encourages domestic production to reduce the trade deficit in the **petrochemical sector**.
 
• **Applications**: Beyond household items, petrochemicals are vital for **healthcare** (medical devices), **telecommunications** (optical fibres), and **renewable energy** (components for **solar panels**).

questions.question: Which constitutional authority decides on the disqualification of a Member of State Legislature under the Anti-Defection Law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker of the Legislative Assembly**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The decision on the disqualification of a member of the State Legislature under the **Anti-Defection Law** is made by the **Presiding Officer** of the House. For the Legislative Assembly, this authority is the **Speaker**, and for the Legislative Council, it is the **Chairperson**. ***Hence, the option involving the Speaker is correct.***
 
• The **Anti-Defection Law** was added to the Constitution of India via the **10th Schedule** through the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in the year **1985**. It was designed to prevent political defections prompted by the lure of office or similar considerations.
 
• According to the **10th Schedule**, any question regarding whether a member of a House has become subject to disqualification shall be referred to the **Speaker** or the **Chairperson** of such House, and their decision shall be final.
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India, in the landmark **Kihoto Hollohan vs Zachillhu case (1992)**, ruled that the decision of the **Speaker** or **Chairperson** is subject to **judicial review** on grounds of malafides or perversity. This means that while the Speaker decides, the **High Court** or **Supreme Court** can later examine the legality of that decision. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Chief Justice deciding initially is incorrect.***
 
• The **Election Commission** of India does not have the primary authority to decide on disqualification under the **10th Schedule**, although it advises the **Governor** on disqualifications arising under **Article 191(1)** (like office of profit or unsound mind). ***Hence, the statement involving the Election Commission in the context of defection is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Grounds for Disqualification:** Under the **10th Schedule**, a member can be disqualified if they **voluntarily give up** the membership of their political party or if they vote (or abstain from voting) in the House contrary to any direction issued by the political party (the **Whip**) without obtaining prior permission or if such act is not condoned within **15 days**.
 
• **Independent and Nominated Members:** An **independent member** becomes disqualified if they join any political party after the election. A **nominated member** is disqualified if they join any political party after the expiry of **6 months** from the date on which they take their seat in the House.
 
• **The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:** This amendment strengthened the law by deleting the provision that protected a "split" (where 1/3rd members defect). Now, at least **two-thirds** of the members of a party must in favour of a **merger** with another party to avoid disqualification.
 
• **Article 191 and 192:** **Article 191(2)** specifically mentions disqualification on the grounds of the **Tenth Schedule**. **Article 192** states that for other disqualifications (like holding an **Office of Profit**), the **Governor** decides after obtaining the opinion of the **Election Commission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **No Time Limit for Decision:** Originally, the **Constitution** did not specify a **time limit** within which the **Speaker** must decide on a disqualification plea. This often led to political delays. However, in the **Keisham Meghachandra Singh case (2020)**, the **Supreme Court** recommended that the **Speaker** should decide such cases within a reasonable period, typically **3 months**.
 
• **Exceptions to the Law:** Disqualification does not apply in the case of a **merger** where **two-thirds** of the members of the legislative party agree to the merger. Also, a person elected as **Speaker** or **Deputy Speaker** can resign from their party and rejoin it after they cease to hold that office without being disqualified.
 
• **Impact on Stability:** The law aims to bring **political stability** to the **government** by ensuring that legislators do not change parties frequently, a practice colloquially known as **"Aaya Ram Gaya Ram"** in the Indian political context which was prevalent before **1985**.

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:
Assertion (A): The Buddha sculptures of the Gandhara School show Hellenistic features.
Reason (R): The Buddha head from this school has curly hair and shows typical Hellenistic elements.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Assertion (A)** states that the **Buddha sculptures** of the **Gandhara School** show **Hellenistic features**. This school of art flourished in the **northwestern part** of the Indian subcontinent (modern-day **Pakistan and Afghanistan**) and was heavily influenced by **Greek and Roman** styles due to its proximity to the **Hellenistic world**. ***Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.***

• **Reason (R)** explains that the **Buddha head** from this school features **curly hair** and other typical **Hellenistic elements**. The **Gandhara Buddha** is often depicted with facial features resembling the **Greek God Apollo**, including a **sharp nose**, **defined lips**, and **wavy hair** tied in a topknot known as the **Ushnisha**. ***Hence, Reason (R) is correct.***

• The specific physical traits mentioned in **Reason (R)**, such as the **anatomical accuracy** and **curly hair**, are the direct reasons why the **Gandhara School** is classified as having **Hellenistic** or **Greco-Buddhist** features.

• The combination of **Buddhist themes** with **foreign techniques** of execution is the hallmark of this school, which emerged during the **1st Century BC** and reached its peak during the **Kushan Empire** under **King Kanishka**.

• ***Hence, both A and R are true, and R provides the correct explanation for A.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Origins and Patronage**:

• The **Gandhara School of Art** developed during the **1st Century BC to 4th Century AD**.

• It received significant patronage from the **Kushan Dynasty**, particularly **King Kanishka**, who was a great promoter of **Mahayana Buddhism**.

• The major centers of this art were **Taxila**, **Peshawar**, and **Bagram**.

• **Materials and Techniques**:

• The early sculptures of the **Gandhara School** were primarily made using **bluish-grey schist stone**.

• In the later phases (around the **3rd and 4th Century AD**), **stucco** (a type of lime-plaster) and **mud** were increasingly used for creating figurines and reliefs.

• The style is characterized by **realistic anatomy**, **muscular representations**, and **heavy drapery** with folds, similar to **Roman togas**.

• **Comparison with Mathura School**:

• Unlike the **Gandhara School**, which was **hybrid** in nature, the **Mathura School** was purely **indigenous** and developed around the same period in **Uttar Pradesh**.

• The **Mathura School** used **spotted red sandstone** as its primary material.

• In **Mathura art**, the **Buddha** was depicted as **stout** and **smiling**, focusing more on spiritual inner joy rather than **Hellenistic physical perfection**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Hellenistic Influence**: The influence of **Alexander the Great’s** conquests and the subsequent **Indo-Greek kingdoms** led to the **amalgamation** of **Greek art** with **Indian religious themes**.

• **Physical Attributes**: The **Buddha** in **Gandhara art** is often shown with a **halo** (Prabhamandala), which sometimes features **geometric patterns**, and his **ears are elongated** to signify his previous life as a **Prince (Siddhartha)** who wore heavy jewelry.

• **Artistic Legacy**: This school is credited with the **first anthropomorphic representation** of the **Buddha** (depicting him in human form), as earlier **Hinayana** traditions used **symbols** like the **Bodhi tree**, **footprints**, or an **empty throne**.

• **Mudras**: The sculptures often depict the **Buddha** in various **Mudras** (hand gestures) such as **Abhaya Mudra** (fearlessness), **Dharmachakra Mudra** (teaching), and **Dhyana Mudra** (meditation).

questions.question: Which of the following situations will result in a point awarded to the defending team in Kabaddi?

options.text: The raider tags two defenders and crosses the midliners
The raider fails to chant "Kabaddi" during the raid
The raider touches the bonus line without being tackled
The defending team crosses the lobby before contact

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The raider fails to chant "Kabaddi" during the raid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **Kabaddi**, the **"Cant"** is the continuous clear chanting of the approved word **"Kabaddi"** by the **raider** in a single breath. If the raider fails to maintain this chant or loses their breath during the **raid**, they are declared **out**, and the **defending team** is awarded **1 point**. *Hence, statement B is correct.*
 
• When a **raider** successfully tags or touches **two defenders** and safely returns to their own half by crossing the **midline**, the **raiding team** is awarded **2 points** (one for each defender touched), and those defenders must leave the mat. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• Touching the **bonus line** is a specific scoring maneuver. If a **raider** crosses the **bonus line** with one foot while the other foot is in the air, and there are **6 or 7 defenders** present on the mat, the **raiding team** receives **1 point**. This does not result in a point for the defense. *Hence, statement C is incorrect.*
 
• The **lobby** area (the yellow strips on the sides) only becomes **"active"** once a touch has been made between the **raider** and a **defender**. If a defender steps into the **lobby** without any contact being initiated, they are considered **"out of bounds,"** and a point is awarded to the **raiding team**. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*
 
• According to the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** rules, a **raid** is unsuccessful if the raider is tackled, goes out of bounds, or commits a **technical foul** like losing the **cant**. In all these cases, the **defending team** earns a point and revives one of their own players.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Court Dimensions and Player Count:** A standard **Kabaddi** court for **men** measures **13 meters by 10 meters**, while for **women** and **juniors**, it is **12 meters by 8 meters**. Each team consists of **12 players**, but only **7 players** are allowed on the **mat** at any given time during the match.
 
• **Super Tackle:** This is a unique scoring rule where if the **defending team** has **3 or fewer defenders** on the mat and they successfully tackle the **raider**, they are awarded **2 points** instead of the usual 1. This is a crucial strategy in modern leagues like the **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**, which began in **2014**.
 
• **Lobby Rule:** The **lobby** is the **1-meter wide** strip on both sides of the court. It is considered part of the playing area only during a **struggle** (after a touch). If a player enters it without a touch, they are **eliminated** from the current round.
 
• **Duration of Match:** A professional match typically lasts for **40 minutes**, divided into two halves of **20 minutes** each, with a **5-minute break** in between. In the **Asian Games**, where **Kabaddi** has been a regular feature since **1990**, these timing rules are strictly followed.
 
• **Types of Kabaddi:** There are two main styles: the **Standard Style** (played on a rectangular mat) and the **Circle Style** (played on a circular field, popular in **Punjab**). The **Pro Kabaddi League** and **World Cup** follow the **Standard Style**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Do-or-Die Raid:** If a team performs **two consecutive empty raids** (raids where no points are scored or lost), the **third raid** is designated as a **"Do-or-Die" raid**. In this raid, the **raider** must score a point (by touch or bonus), or they will be declared **out**, even if they are not tackled.
 
• **Raid Time Limit:** Every **raid** has a maximum duration of **30 seconds**. If the **raider** fails to return to their half within this **30-second** window, they are ruled **out**, and the **defending team** receives a point.
 
• **All-Out (Lona):** When a team manages to eliminate all **7 players** of the opposing team, they score an **"All-Out,"** which awards **2 bonus points** in addition to the points earned for the individual touches. All eliminated players of the opposing team are then **revived**.
 
• **Technical Points:** Points can also be awarded for **coaching violations**, **wrong substitutions**, or if a defender pulls the **raider's hair** or clothes. These are called **technical points** and do not result in the **revival** of a player.
</ul

__
 
• **Raziyya Sultan** (also known as **Razia Sultana**) reigned from **1236** to **1240**. She was the first and only female ruler of the **Delhi Sultanate**. Her reign lasted for approximately **4 years**. ***Hence, statement B is correct.***
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq** ascended the throne in **1325** and ruled until his death in **1351**. His total reign spanned **26 years**, during which he was known for ambitious yet controversial administrative experiments. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Alauddin Khalji**, the most powerful ruler of the **Khalji dynasty**, reigned from **1296** to **1316**. His rule lasted for **20 years** and was characterized by massive territorial expansion and economic reforms in **India**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban** served as the Sultan of **Delhi** from **1266** to **1287**. His reign lasted for **21 years**. He is credited with consolidating the power of the **Mamluk dynasty** through his policy of **"Iron and Blood."** ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Raziyya Sultan:** She was the daughter of **Iltutmish**, who nominated her as his successor over his sons. Despite being an able administrator and a brave warrior, she faced heavy opposition from the **Turkish nobility** (the **Chahalgani**) because she was a woman. She was eventually defeated and killed near **Kaithal** in the year **1240**.
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq:** Often referred to as a **"wise fool"** by historians like **Ibn Battuta**, he introduced **token currency** in **1329** and ordered the transfer of the capital from **Delhi** to **Devagiri** (renamed **Daulatabad**). These projects resulted in significant economic loss and administrative chaos.
 
• **Alauddin Khalji:** He was the first Sultan to invade **South India**, led by his general **Malik Kafur**. He introduced strict **price control** mechanisms and market regulations to maintain a large standing army. He also built the **Alai Darwaza** and the city of **Siri** in **Delhi**.
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban:** He introduced the Persian customs of **Sijda** (prostration) and **Paibos** (kissing the Sultan's feet) to elevate the status of the monarch. He established a separate military department called **Diwan-i-Arz** to strengthen the internal security of the **Delhi Sultanate** against **Mongol** invasions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Delhi Sultanate** comprised five successive dynasties: the **Mamluk/Slave Dynasty** (**1206–1290**), the **Khalji Dynasty** (**1290–1320**), the **Tughlaq Dynasty** (**1320–1414**), the **Sayyid Dynasty** (**1414–1451**), and the **Lodi Dynasty** (**1451–1526**).
 
• The **Slave Dynasty** was established by **Qutb-ud-din Aibak**, a former slave of **Muhammad Ghori**, in the year **1206**.
 
• The **Tughlaq Dynasty** enjoyed the longest period of rule among all the Sultanate dynasties, lasting for nearly **94 years**, while the **Khalji Dynasty** had the shortest span of approximately **30 years**.
 
• The **Sultanate period** ended in **1526** with the **First Battle of Panipat**, where **Babur** defeated **Ibrahim Lodi**, leading to the foundation of the **Mughal Empire** in **India**.

questions.question:
Match the atmospheric phenomenon with its primary measurement instrument
1. Wind Speed
2. Humidity
3. Atmospheric Pressure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1-Anemometer, 2-Hygrometer, 3-Barometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anemometer**: This is a **scientific instrument** used to measure **wind speed** and **wind pressure**. It is a fundamental tool for **meteorologists** who study weather patterns and for **physicists** who study the way air moves. The first description of an anemometer was given by **Leon Battista Alberti** around **1450**. *Hence, the match for wind speed is correct.*
 
• **Hygrometer**: A **hygrometer** is an instrument used to measure the **amount of water vapor** in the atmosphere, in soil, or in confined spaces. Humidity measurement is vital in **meteorology**, **agriculture**, and **industrial manufacturing**. The concept of the hygrometer dates back to the **15th century**, with significant improvements made by **Horace Bénédict de Saussure** in **1783** using a human hair to measure humidity. *Hence, the match for humidity is correct.*
 
• **Barometer**: A **barometer** is an instrument used to measure **atmospheric pressure**. Because atmospheric pressure changes with distance above or below sea level, a barometer can also be used to measure **altitude**. **Evangelista Torricelli**, an Italian physicist and mathematician, is generally credited with inventing the mercury barometer in **1643**. *Hence, the match for atmospheric pressure is correct.*
 
• The combination of these instruments allows for **weather forecasting** and the monitoring of **climatic conditions** across different **geographical locations**. *Hence, the statement representing option C is the correct match.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wind Speed Measurement (Anemometer)**:
 
 
• There are several types of anemometers, including the **Cup Anemometer**, which consists of four cups that rotate with the wind, and the **Sonic Anemometer**, which uses **ultrasonic sound waves** to measure wind velocity.
 
• In addition to speed, a **Wind Vane** is often paired with an anemometer to determine the **direction** of the wind.
 
• These instruments are critical at **airports** for aviation safety and at **wind farms** to optimize **energy production**.
 
 
 
• **Humidity Measurement (Hygrometer)**:
 
 
• **Relative Humidity (RH)** is the most common way to express the amount of moisture in the air relative to the maximum amount the air could hold at that **temperature**.
 
• A **Psychrometer** is a specific type of hygrometer that uses two **thermometers** (one dry bulb and one wet bulb) to determine humidity through the **cooling effect of evaporation**.
 
• Modern **digital hygrometers** use **capacitive** or **resistive** sensors to measure moisture levels in **HVAC systems** and **museums** to preserve artifacts.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure Measurement (Barometer)**:
 
 
• There are two main types of barometers: **Mercury Barometers** and **Aneroid Barometers**. The aneroid version is more portable and uses a small, flexible **metal box** called an aneroid cell.
 
• Atmospheric pressure is commonly measured in units of **hectopascals (hPa)**, **millibars (mb)**, or **inches of mercury (inHg)**.
 
• A **rising barometer** generally indicates **fair weather**, while a **falling barometer** suggests approaching **storms** or low-pressure systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Standard Atmospheric Pressure**: At **sea level**, the standard atmospheric pressure is approximately **1013.25 hPa** (or 14.7 pounds per square inch).
 
• **Instrument Calibration**: All meteorological instruments require regular **calibration** against **international standards** to ensure accuracy in global **weather reports** and **climate models**.
 
• **Other Meteorological Instruments**: Apart from the ones mentioned, a **Thermometer** is used for measuring temperature, and a **Rain Gauge** (or **Ombrometer**) is used to measure **liquid precipitation** over a set period.
 
• **Historical Context**: The development of these instruments during the **Scientific Revolution** in the **17th and 18th centuries** laid the groundwork for modern **meteorology**.
